title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance refers to how much the model's predictions would change if we used a different training dataset.

title: Effect of More Data on Bias
text: Adding more data points generally helps in reducing variance but does not necessarily affect bias. Bias is more related to the model's assumptions.

title: Model Complexity and Bias
text: A more complex model can capture more patterns in the data, potentially reducing bias. However, the given model's complexity is fixed, and adding more data does not change this.

title: Evaluating the Statement
text: Does collecting more data points change the model's assumptions or complexity?
